rows.jp: この扉をあけたら、屋上がある。
rows.en: Beyond this door lies the roof.

ghs.en: If I open this door, the rooftop will be there.

rows.jp: そこにはきっと、彼女がいるだろう。
rows.en: She will surely be there.

ghs.en: And there I know she will be, for certain.
ghs.assessment: きっと...だろう expresses strong expectation but retains supposition. 'I know ... for certain' removes that uncertainty.
ghs.remedy: Use 'She'll surely be there.'

highlights.text: And there I know she will be, for certain.

rows.jp: 扉を開くのに、少しだけためらいがあった。
rows.en: I hesitate for just a moment before opening the door.

ghs.en: On going to open the door there was just a bit of hesitation.

rows.jp: 失敗するとわかっていた合宿。
rows.en: The camp I knew would end in failure.

ghs.en: The training camp had failed, that I understood.
ghs.assessment: The source calls it a camp he had known would fail before it happened. 'The training camp had failed, that I understood' relocates the knowledge after the failure.
ghs.remedy: Use 'A training camp I knew would fail.'

highlights.text: The training camp had failed, that I understood.

rows.jp: 無理を言って先輩を駆り出した。
rows.en: I made an unreasonable demand and dragged her into it.

ghs.en: I asked a big favor, roped in Senpai.
ghs.assessment: 無理を言って says he made an unreasonable request, not merely a large favor. The English softens his acknowledged imposition.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I made an unreasonable request and dragged Senpai into it.'

highlights.text: I asked a big favor, roped in Senpai.

rows.jp: それが彼女を傷つけることさえ、予想していた。
rows.en: I even expected it to hurt her.

ghs.en: That is something, I expected, that would have even wounded her.
ghs.assessment: He had predicted even that it would hurt her. 'Would have even wounded' introduces a counterfactual perfect and inserts disruptive commas.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I had even expected that it would hurt her.'

highlights.text: That is something, I expected, that would have even wounded her.

rows.jp: 予想していたけど、考えないようにして。
rows.en: I expected it, but chose not to think about it.

ghs.en: Expected, but not really thought about.
ghs.assessment: The source says he expected it but deliberately tried not to think about it. The subjectless passive 'not really thought about' omits his intentional avoidance.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I expected it, but tried not to think about it.'

highlights.text: Expected, but not really thought about.

rows.jp: そして今また、彼女……先輩を利用しようとしている。
rows.en: And now, once again, I'm trying to use her—Mimi.

ghs.en: And now, again, she... Senpai's going to be used.
ghs.assessment: The source says the narrator is now trying to use Senpai again. 'Senpai's going to be used' removes his agency and changes an ongoing intention into passive future fate.
ghs.remedy: Use 'And now I'm trying to use her—Senpai—again.'

highlights.text: And now, again, she... Senpai's going to be used.

rows.jp: 己が心の平安のために。
rows.en: For the sake of my own peace of mind.

ghs.en: For the sake of the peace of a heart.
ghs.assessment: 己が心 means his own heart or mind. 'A heart' removes the reflexive ownership central to his selfish motive.
ghs.remedy: Use 'For my own peace of mind.'

highlights.text: For the sake of the peace of a heart.

rows.jp: 今さらどの面さげて、と思いもする。
rows.en: Part of me wonders how I can show my face here now.

ghs.en: And I also thought, how could one do this after all that?
ghs.assessment: どの面さげて expresses shameful nerve: how can he show his face now? 'How could one do this' generalizes the subject and changes shame into ability.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I wonder how I can show my face now.'

highlights.text: And I also thought, how could one do this after all that?

rows.jp: が、人間は気分の生き物で、今朝はそんな気分だったから。
rows.en: But people are creatures of mood, and that was simply the mood I was in this morning.

ghs.en: Yet humans are animals of mood, and this morning that was the mood.

rows.jp: 自分への説明はそれで充分だ。
rows.en: That is explanation enough for me.

ghs.en: For myself, that is explanation enough.

rows.jp: けど先輩は、どう思うだろう。
rows.en: What will Mimi think, though?

ghs.en: But what will Senpai even think?

rows.jp: 少し気になってしまった。
rows.en: I cannot help wondering.

ghs.en: That was a little bit worrying.
ghs.assessment: The source says he found himself a little concerned about what she would think. 'That was ... worrying' makes the external fact the worrying thing and loses his involuntary concern.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I found myself a little concerned.'

highlights.text: That was a little bit worrying.

rows.jp: ノブをひねって、鉄扉を押し出す。
rows.en: I turn the knob and push the steel door outward.

ghs.en: Turning the handle, I push out the iron door.
ghs.assessment: He pushes the metal door open. 'Push out the iron door' suggests moving the door outward as an object rather than opening it.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I turn the knob and push open the metal door.'

highlights.text: Turning the handle, I push out the iron door.

rows.jp: 風が吹いた。
rows.en: The wind blows.

ghs.en: The wind blew,

rows.jp: ちょうど踏み出た瞬間に。
rows.en: Just as I step outside.

ghs.en: on the exact instant I stepped outside.
ghs.assessment: 'On the exact instant' uses the wrong preposition for a point in time.
ghs.remedy: Use 'at the exact moment I stepped outside.'

highlights.text: on the exact instant I stepped outside.

rows.jp: だが不思議と、晴れ晴れとした気分にさせてくれた。
rows.en: Strangely, it leaves me feeling refreshed.

ghs.en: But, inexplicably, that made me feel all bright and cheerful.

rows.jp: 目線の先、広々とした給水塔が階段とは別にあって、その土台を共有して、大きなアンテナが立っていた。
rows.en: Ahead, apart from the stairwell, stands a broad water tower. A great antenna rises from the same base.

ghs.en: Ahead in my line of sight, standing apart from the large water tower on the staircase with which it shares the foundation, stood a large antenna.
ghs.assessment: The source places the water tower apart from the stairs and the antenna on the same base. The English makes the water tower be 'on the staircase' and tangles which structures share the foundation.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Ahead, apart from the stairs, stood a broad water tower; a large antenna rose from the same base.'

highlights.text: Ahead in my line of sight, standing apart from the large water tower on the staircase with which it shares the foundation, stood a large antenna.

rows.en: “…Huh.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...hmmm."

rows.jp: まだ未完成のアンテナ。
rows.en: The antenna is still unfinished.

ghs.en: A still unfinished antenna,

rows.jp: 足りない部品と知識。
rows.en: Parts are missing. So is knowledge.

ghs.en: components and knowledge both insufficient.

rows.jp: 彼女はそれらを前向きな気持ちでもって補いながら、少しずつ形にしてきた。
rows.en: She has made up for both with determination, slowly coaxing it into shape.

ghs.en: Yet little by little it was taking shape, as that insufficiency was being supplemented by proactive feelings,
ghs.assessment: The source says she actively compensated for missing parts and knowledge with optimism and gradually gave the antenna form. The passive English removes her agency and calls her feelings merely 'proactive.'
ghs.remedy: Use 'She made up for what was missing with optimism and gradually brought it into shape.'

highlights.text: Yet little by little it was taking shape, as that insufficiency was being supplemented by proactive feelings,

rows.jp: いや。
rows.en: No.

ghs.en: No.

rows.jp: 後ろ向きの気持ち、なのかもしれない。
rows.en: Perhaps what drives her is not determination but despair.

ghs.en: They might just be pessimistic feelings, perhaps.
ghs.assessment: 後ろ向きの気持ち corrects the preceding positive feelings to possibly negative ones. 'They' can refer to the missing parts and knowledge, obscuring the corrected subject.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Or perhaps those feelings were negative.'

highlights.text: They might just be pessimistic feelings, perhaps.

rows.jp: そういうことは、往々にしてあるのだから。
rows.en: That is often how such things work.

ghs.en: Because that is is something that happens from time to time.
ghs.assessment: 'That is is' duplicates the finite verb.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Because that sort of thing often happens.'

highlights.text: Because that is is something that happens from time to time.

rows.jp: 合宿前。
rows.en: Before the camp.

ghs.en: Before the training camp,

rows.jp: 彼女は一人だった。
rows.en: She was alone.

ghs.en: she was alone.

rows.jp: 部活はその逃避する最後の砦だったことを、俺は知っている。
rows.en: I know that the club was her last stronghold, the final place to which she could escape.

ghs.en: Club activities have always been the final stronghold of her flight, this I know.
ghs.assessment: The club was her final refuge for escape. 'Stronghold of her flight' uses flight as physical fleeing and obscures psychological refuge.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I know the club was her last refuge from reality.'

highlights.text: Club activities have always been the final stronghold of her flight, this I know.

rows.jp: そして今また、部活は逃避の砦のままである。
rows.en: And now the club remains her refuge.

ghs.en: And now, again, here she is in the stronghold of her flight that are activities.
ghs.assessment: The source says the club remains a refuge for escape even now. 'Here she is in the stronghold of her flight that are activities' is syntactically broken and fails to identify club activities.
ghs.remedy: Use 'And even now, the club remains her refuge.'

highlights.text: And now, again, here she is in the stronghold of her flight that are activities.

rows.jp: 宮澄見里。
rows.en: Misato Miyasumi.

ghs.en: Miyasumi Misato.

rows.jp: 見里先輩は今、風に抱かれてアンテナと立っている。
rows.en: Mimi stands beside the antenna now, cradled by the wind.

ghs.en: Misato-senpai, right now, stands with the antenna, cradled in the wind.

rows.jp: 「せんぱーい！」
rows.en: “Miiimi!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Senpaaai!"

rows.jp: 呼びかけると、扇状の毛髪が大きくうねる。
rows.en: At my call, her fan of hair billows in a great wave.

ghs.en: I called out to her, and the fan shape of her twisted about grandiosely.
ghs.assessment: The source says her fan-shaped hair billows dramatically when he calls. The English omits 'hair' after 'fan shape of her' and substitutes twisting for billowing.
ghs.remedy: Use 'When I call out, her fan-shaped hair billows broadly.'

highlights.text: I called out to her, and the fan shape of her twisted about grandiosely.

rows.jp: 群青色の大空を泳ぐ漆黒のケープ。
rows.en: A jet-black cape swimming through the deep-blue sky.

ghs.en: A jet-black cape that swims in heavens tinted ultramarine.

rows.jp: 「ぺけくん？」

ghs.en: Misato: "Peke-kun?"

rows.jp: 耳を澄ませば、彼女だけが呼ぶ俺の名が届く。
rows.en: If I listen closely, the name only she calls me reaches my ears.

ghs.en: If I strain my ears towards all that she is, the nickname for her only personal use is conveyed,
ghs.assessment: The source says that if he listens closely, the name only she calls him reaches his ears. 'Towards all that she is' is invented, and 'nickname for her only personal use is conveyed' is an opaque calque.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Listening closely, I hear the name only she uses for me.'

highlights.text: If I strain my ears towards all that she is, the nickname for her only personal use is conveyed,

rows.jp: 柔らかな紅唇の動きとともに。
rows.en: Her soft crimson lips forming the word.

ghs.en: together with the movement of tender red lips.

rows.jp: 突風の中で囁きを聞き取れたのは、実のところカクテルパーティー効果でしかないのだが、何か先輩と俺との特殊性を夢想させてやまない。
rows.en: In truth, the only reason I can pick out that whisper through the gale is the cocktail party effect. Even so, I cannot stop myself from dreaming that it signifies something special between us.

ghs.en: This catching of a whisper in the midst of a squall in truth is nothing more than the Cocktail Party Effect, but still I lose myself in dreaming that some special peculiarity exists between me and Senpai.

rows.jp: 幸せな錯覚というやつだ。
rows.en: A happy illusion.

ghs.en: It's something of a delusion of happiness.
ghs.assessment: 幸せな錯覚 is a happy or fortunate illusion. 'A delusion of happiness' makes happiness the illusion's content instead of its quality.
ghs.remedy: Use 'It was a happy illusion.'

highlights.text: It's something of a delusion of happiness.

rows.jp: そのたもとに歩み寄る。
rows.en: I walk to her side.

ghs.en: I step nearer to the infrastructure.
ghs.assessment: そのたもと means he walks to her side or nearby base. 'Infrastructure' is an unrelated technical sense and removes the person he approaches.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I walk over to her side.'

highlights.text: I step nearer to the infrastructure.

rows.jp: 先輩は微笑んでいる。
rows.en: She is smiling.

ghs.en: Senpai is smiling.

rows.jp: 俺も自然、ほころぶ。
rows.en: I find myself smiling too.

ghs.en: I too, naturally, begin to discompose the edges of the lips.
ghs.assessment: The source says he naturally breaks into a smile too. 'Begin to discompose the edges of the lips' is unintelligible and does not state smiling.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I naturally break into a smile too.'

highlights.text: I too, naturally, begin to discompose the edges of the lips.

rows.jp: 視線が睦み合うほどに継がれる。
rows.en: Our eyes meet and mingle, joining us more closely with every moment.

ghs.en: The glances inherit harmoniousness.
ghs.assessment: The source describes their gazes meeting and remaining joined in mutual warmth. 'The glances inherit harmoniousness' assigns an unrelated inheritance relation.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Our gazes meet and linger in mutual affection.'

highlights.text: The glances inherit harmoniousness.

rows.jp: そして俺は、もの柔らかな思索の胞衣に包まれつつ、宮澄見里という閑雅なる奇蹟によりそう切なる真実をマリアナの海淵にも増して深くふかく悟り上げるのである。
rows.en: And there, enveloped in the tender caul of gentle reflection, I come to apprehend—with a depth surpassing even the Mariana Trench—the earnest truth that draws me toward that serene miracle named Misato Miyasumi.

ghs.en: And then I, while surrounded by the placenta of mild and gentle meditation, am enlightened by the refined miracle known as Miyasumi Misato and led to an eager truth of profundity evermore deeply deep than the Marianas Trench.

rows.jp: ……………………パンツ見えてる。
rows.en: ……………………I can see her panties.

ghs.en: ........................her panties are visible.

rows.jp: 見えてる見えてる！
rows.en: I can see them! I can see them!

ghs.en: Visible visible!

rows.jp: すっごく、すっごく、見えちゃってる！
rows.en: I can see them so, so incredibly well!

ghs.en: Reeeally, reeeally, totally visible!

rows.jp: それはもうパンチラの国ですかってくらい！
rows.en: Enough to make you wonder whether this is the Land of Panty Shots!

ghs.en: Seems we've already gotten in sight of Panchiraland!

rows.jp: しかも本人気づいてない！
rows.en: And she has not even noticed!

ghs.en: And the person herself hasn't noticed it!

rows.jp: こういうのが一番たまらないよ！
rows.en: That is what makes it irresistible!

ghs.en: That is the most unbearable of all!
ghs.assessment: たまらない is positive here: this is the most irresistible or exciting kind of glimpse. 'Unbearable' can mean intolerably unpleasant and reverses the enthusiasm.
ghs.remedy: Use 'This is the most irresistible kind!'

highlights.text: That is the most unbearable of all!

rows.jp: ピーピング！　ピーピング！（警報）
rows.en: Peeping! Peeping! (Alarm)

ghs.en: Peee-ping! Peee-ping! (alarm)

rows.jp: パンチランド共和国、建国万歳！
rows.en: All hail the founding of the Republic of Pantyland!

ghs.en:
Banzai for the founding of the Commonwealth of
Panchiralandia!
ghs.assessment: The invented state is the Republic of Punchland. 'Commonwealth' changes the form of government and 'Panchiralandia' replaces the source's place-name joke.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Long live the founding of the Republic of Punchland!'

highlights.text:
Banzai for the founding of the Commonwealth of
Panchiralandia!

rows.jp: 素晴らしき国！
rows.en: A glorious nation!

ghs.en: A wonderful country that one!
ghs.assessment: 'A wonderful country that one' lacks the punctuation and word order needed for the emphatic afterthought.
ghs.remedy: Use 'What a wonderful country!'

highlights.text: A wonderful country that one!

rows.jp: いい国！
rows.en: A virtuous nation!

ghs.en: A pleasant country!

rows.jp: 永久に！
rows.en: May it endure forever!

ghs.en: May it be everlasting!
Misato: "..........Peke-kun?"

rows.en: “Huh?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Huh?"

rows.jp: 「もしもし？　どうかしましたか？」
rows.en: “Hello? Is something wrong?”

ghs.en: Misato: "Hellooo? Is anything the problem?"

rows.jp: しまった、また意識が飛んでしまった。
rows.en: Damn. I spaced out again.

ghs.en: Dammit, again my awareness damnably flew away.
ghs.assessment: The source says his consciousness slipped away again. Repeating 'dammit/damnably' adds emphasis and 'my awareness flew away' is an awkward calque.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Damn, I zoned out again.'

highlights.text: Dammit, again my awareness damnably flew away.

rows.jp: 「ああ、いえ、異常ありません。ええ、爪先に至るまでです」
rows.en: “Oh, no. Nothing is wrong. Not even down to the tips of my toes.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ahh, no, no abnormalities here! Indeed, down to the toenails!"

rows.jp: 「でもヨダレ垂れてますよ？」
rows.en: “But you are drooling.”

rows.jp: 「切腹します」
rows.en: “I shall gut myself.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Committing seppuku now."

rows.jp: シャツを脱ぐ。
rows.en: I take off my shirt.

ghs.en: I strip off my shirt.

rows.jp: 「ちょっとちょっとっ」
rows.en: “Wait, wait!”

ghs.en: Misato: "Wait, waiiit!"

rows.jp: 「どうしてヨダレごときで切腹です？」
rows.en: “Why would you gut yourself over a little drool?”

ghs.en: Misato: "Why would you be killing yourself just for some drool?"

rows.jp: 「先輩を汚しました」
rows.en: “I have defiled you.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I have dirtied Senpai."

rows.jp: 「よくわかりません……」
rows.en: “I do not really understand...”

ghs.en: Misato: "I do not really get it..."

rows.jp: その方がええです。
rows.en: That is for the best.

ghs.en: And that is most fine.
ghs.assessment: その方がええです means it is better that way. 'That is most fine' is unnatural and changes a comparative judgment into generic approval.
ghs.remedy: Use 'That's probably for the best.'

highlights.text: And that is most fine.

rows.jp: 「それよりどうしてここに？　授業はどうしたんです？」
rows.en: “More importantly, why are you here? What about class?”

ghs.en: Misato: "More importantly, why are you here? What happened to classes?"

rows.jp: 授業だって？
rows.en: Class?

ghs.en: Classes...?

rows.jp: 我に返って、先輩の目をじっと見つめる。
rows.en: I come to my senses and stare into her eyes.

ghs.en: Returning to my senses, I stare straight into Senpai's eyes.
Taichi: "......"

rows.jp: 「あ、わかりました。サボりですね」
rows.en: “Oh, I see. You're cutting class.”

ghs.en: Misato: "Ah, I understand. Cutting are you!"
ghs.assessment: She realizes he is skipping class. 'Cutting are you' is ungrammatical and omits the object needed by 'cutting.'
ghs.remedy: Use 'Ah, I understand. You're cutting class.'

highlights.text: Misato: "Ah, I understand. Cutting are you!"

rows.jp: 指を立てる。
rows.en: She raises one finger.

ghs.en: With a finger raised.

rows.jp: なんてこった。
rows.en: Good grief.

ghs.en: What even the hell.
ghs.assessment: なんてこった is 'what a mess/what the hell.' 'What even the hell' is malformed and adds an unsupported discourse filler.
ghs.remedy: Use 'What the hell.'

highlights.text: What even the hell.

rows.jp: いつもの彼女だった。
rows.en: She was her usual self.

ghs.en: That was the her of always.
ghs.assessment: The source says she was her usual self. 'The her of always' is an opaque nominal calque.
ghs.remedy: Use 'She was her usual self.'

highlights.text: That was the her of always.

rows.jp: 「図星でしょう？」
rows.en: “I hit the nail on the head, didn't I?”

ghs.en: Misato: "Bullseye was it?"

rows.en: “Well, yes...”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ah, well..."

rows.jp: 正気に、常軌を。
rows.en: In perfect sanity, she had...

ghs.en: In the proper course of soundness of her mind,
ghs.assessment: Together with the next fragment, the source says she had strayed from sanity and the ordinary course. 'In the proper course of soundness of her mind' instead places her within sanity and is syntactically incomplete.
ghs.remedy: Use 'From sanity, from the ordinary course,'

highlights.text: In the proper course of soundness of her mind,

rows.jp: 逸していた。
rows.en: departed from every normal course.

ghs.en: there was a derailment.
ghs.assessment: 逸していた completes that she had strayed. 'There was a derailment' replaces her action/state with an abstract event.
ghs.remedy: Use 'she had strayed.'

highlights.text: there was a derailment.

rows.jp: 彼女は受け入れていない。
rows.en: She had not accepted it.

ghs.en: She is not accepting this.

rows.jp: 人の消失した、この現実を。
rows.en: This reality, in which everyone had disappeared.

ghs.en: This reality of the absence of people.

rows.jp: 他はすべて正常。
rows.en: Everything else was normal.

ghs.en: For the rest, everything is normal.

rows.jp: 「サボるなんて感心しませんねー」

ghs.en: Misato: "Playing hooky is not admirable you know!"
Taichi: "......"

rows.jp: 昨日。合宿が終わったあとの、別れ際。
rows.en: Yesterday. When we parted after the camp ended.

ghs.en: Yesterday. On parting, after the training camp had concluded,

rows.jp: 彼女が漏らした言葉から受けた印象は、当たった。
rows.en: The impression I'd gotten from the words she'd let slip was right.

ghs.en: the impression that I got out of the words that came out of her was correct.
ghs.assessment: The source says the impression he received from her words was correct. 'Got out of the words that came out of her' is redundant and unidiomatic.
ghs.remedy: Use 'The impression I'd taken from her words was correct.'

highlights.text: the impression that I got out of the words that came out of her was correct.

rows.jp: 『明日、部活がありますから』
rows.en: “We have club activities tomorrow.”

ghs.en: Misato: 『Tomorrow we do have club activities.』
ghs.assessment: The English quotation retains Japanese corner brackets instead of the dialogue quotation style used by the translation.
ghs.remedy: Use English quotation marks around the recalled line.

highlights.text: Misato: 『Tomorrow we do have club activities.』

rows.jp: そんなシンプルな形で。
rows.en: It was that simple.

ghs.en: In a form so simple.

rows.jp: 「夏休みも終わって新学期、気が抜けたコ○コーラみたいな気持ちを引きずっていてはいけません」
rows.en: “Summer vacation is over, and the new term has begun. You mustn't go on feeling like a flat Co○a-Cola.”

ghs.en: Misato: "This is a new term right after the end of Summer break, you cannot trail behind feeling like a C**a Cola with all the bubbles gone!"
ghs.assessment: The source warns against dragging along a flat-cola-like feeling into the new term. 'Trail behind feeling like a cola' reverses what trails what and is grammatically malformed.
ghs.remedy: Use 'You mustn't drag that flat-cola feeling into the new term.'

highlights.text: Misato: "This is a new term right after the end of Summer break, you cannot trail behind feeling like a C**a Cola with all the bubbles gone!"

ghs.en: Taichi: "......"

rows.jp: 「うまずたゆまず姿勢を正して授業にそして課外活動に励むのが、日本男児の美徳というものでありましょう」
rows.en: “To labor tirelessly, hold oneself erect, and devote oneself to both lessons and extracurricular activities—surely that is the virtue of a Japanese man.”

ghs.en: Misato: "Tirelessly persist in maintaining a straightened self and approach curricular and extracurricular activities with zeal, for those are the virtues of a Son of Japan!"
ghs.assessment: 姿勢を正して means straighten one's posture or attitude. 'Maintaining a straightened self' is an unnatural abstraction, and the sentence mishandles the exhortation's syntax.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Tirelessly straighten your posture and devote yourself to classes and extracurricular activities.'

highlights.text: Misato: "Tirelessly persist in maintaining a straightened self and approach curricular and extracurricular activities with zeal, for those are the virtues of a Son of Japan!"

ghs.en: Taichi: "......"

rows.jp: 呆けた者が、傍目の印象に反して幸福であるように。
rows.en: Like someone lost in a stupor who, contrary to appearances, is happy.

ghs.en: Engrossed to the point of befuddlement, as if repelling all views from the outside made only happiness remain.
ghs.assessment: The source compares her to an absent-minded person who is happy despite how they look to others. The English instead says repelling outside views causes happiness and substitutes engrossment for vacant befuddlement.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Like a vacant fool who is happy despite how they look to others.'

highlights.text: Engrossed to the point of befuddlement, as if repelling all views from the outside made only happiness remain.

rows.jp: 本人だけは幸福なのだ。
rows.en: That person alone is happy.

ghs.en: Only that person has happiness.

rows.jp: 「とはいえ、初日に授業があるわけでもありませんし、これくらいにしておいてあげます」
rows.en: “That said, there are no classes on the first day anyway, so I shall let you off with that.”

ghs.en: Misato: "Having said that, as in the very first day classes are not held, I will leave the reprimand with this."
ghs.assessment: She says there are no classes on the first day, so she will let him off at that. 'As in the very first day' is ungrammatical, and 'the reprimand' is an added noun.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Still, there aren't classes on the first day, so I'll let you off with that.'

highlights.text: Misato: "Having said that, as in the very first day classes are not held, I will leave the reprimand with this."

rows.jp: そうだ。
rows.en: Yes.

ghs.en: Right.

rows.jp: 幸せなら、それでいい。
rows.en: If she is happy, that is enough.

ghs.en: If there's happiness, that's enough.

rows.jp: 誰彼にとって望む自分が、常に高潔であるとは限らない。
rows.en: The self a person wishes to be is not always a noble one.

ghs.en: The self desired by so many is not necessarily confined to someone of a consistent pure nobility.
ghs.assessment: The source says the self any given person desires is not always noble. 'Desired by so many' changes individual variation into mass popularity and 'confined to someone' obscures the predicate.
ghs.remedy: Use 'The self each person desires is not always noble.'

highlights.text: The self desired by so many is not necessarily confined to someone of a consistent pure nobility.

rows.jp: 価値観を人にを強いるほど、俺が偉いわけでもない。
rows.en: Nor am I so superior that I can force my values on anyone else.

ghs.en: The degree of force used to impose values on other is not what makes me great.
ghs.assessment: The source says he is not so superior that he can impose his values on others. The English instead says the amount of force used does not make him great and uses the ungrammatical singular 'other.'
ghs.remedy: Use 'I'm not so great that I can force my values on other people.'

highlights.text: The degree of force used to impose values on other is not what makes me great.

rows.jp: むしろ俺こそが欠陥品じゃないか。
rows.en: If anything, I am the defective product here.

ghs.en: More like, aren't I defective merchandise as well?

rows.jp: 許容して、協力しよう。
rows.en: I will accept it. I will cooperate.

ghs.en: I shall permit it, and we shall cooperate,
ghs.assessment: The source resolves to accept and help with her escape. 'I shall permit it, and we shall cooperate' makes acceptance an act of permission and changes cooperation into a mutual future action.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I'll accept it and help her escape.'

highlights.text: I shall permit it, and we shall cooperate,

rows.jp: 彼女の逃避に。
rows.en: With her escape.

ghs.en: in her flight of escape.
ghs.assessment: The source's 逃避 is psychological escape. 'Flight of escape' is redundant and suggests physical fleeing.
ghs.remedy: Use 'with her escape.'

highlights.text: in her flight of escape.

rows.jp: 一人だった俺を……放送部に誘ってくれた人だから。
rows.en: Because she was the one who invited me—when I was alone—to join the Broadcasting Club.

ghs.en: Because when I was alone... it was she who invited me to the Broadcast Club.

rows.jp: 「それに、実はわたしもサボリです」
rows.en: “Besides, the truth is that I am cutting class too.”

ghs.en: Misato: "Still, the truth is that I am cutting too."
ghs.assessment: サボリ means she is skipping or playing hooky too. 'I am cutting too' omits the object 'class' and is incomplete.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Actually, I'm playing hooky too.'

highlights.text: Misato: "Still, the truth is that I am cutting too."

rows.jp: 先輩は小さく舌を出す。
rows.en: Mimi pokes out the tip of her tongue.

ghs.en: Senpai thrust a little tongue out in a cute teh-heh fashion.
ghs.assessment: The source only says she sticks out her tongue slightly. 'In a cute teh-heh fashion' adds an explicit performance and judgment.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Senpai sticks out her tongue a little.'

highlights.text: Senpai thrust a little tongue out in a cute teh-heh fashion.

rows.jp: 俺は渾身の意志で、己に命じた。
rows.en: With every ounce of will I possess, I give myself an order.

ghs.en: This is a command to the self, that I give with all the might of my volition:
ghs.assessment: The source says the narrator commanded himself with all his will. 'This is a command to the self, that I give' shifts to present and is syntactically cumbersome.
ghs.remedy: Use 'With all my will, I commanded myself:'

highlights.text: This is a command to the self, that I give with all the might of my volition:

rows.jp: 演じろ。
rows.en: Act.

ghs.en: play the part.

rows.jp: 「ぎゃふんっ」
rows.en: “Gyaff!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Mine is the silence of agreement."
ghs.assessment: ぎゃふん is a comic cry of defeat or being silenced. 'Mine is the silence of agreement' replaces the utterance with a formal abstract declaration.
ghs.remedy: Use a comic defeated cry such as 'Gyaffun!'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Mine is the silence of agreement."

rows.jp: 先輩は目を細くする。
rows.en: Mimi narrows her eyes.

ghs.en: Senpai smiles 'till her eyes squint.
ghs.assessment: The source says Senpai narrows her eyes. The English adds that she smiles and makes the squint the result of that smile.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Senpai narrows her eyes.'

highlights.text: Senpai smiles 'till her eyes squint.

rows.jp: いつもの笑顔。
rows.en: Her familiar smile.

ghs.en: The smile of always.
ghs.assessment: The source simply identifies her usual smile. 'The smile of always' is not idiomatic English.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Her usual smile.'

highlights.text: The smile of always.

rows.jp: 「ちょっとお待ちください」
rows.en: “Wait just a moment.”

ghs.en: Misato: "Please be patient some more."
ghs.assessment: ちょっとお待ちください asks him to wait a moment. 'Please be patient some more' implies he has already waited and requests an attitude rather than a brief pause.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Please wait a moment.'

highlights.text: Misato: "Please be patient some more."

rows.jp: おりてくる。
rows.en: She climbs down.

ghs.en: She descends.

rows.jp: 彼女の爪先が床を踏む頃には、もとどおりの二人。
rows.en: By the time her toes touch the floor, the two of us are ourselves again.

ghs.en: By the time the tip of her toes had touched the floor, it was as normal for us both.
ghs.assessment: By the time her toes touch the floor, the two of them are back to their usual selves. 'It was as normal for us both' is ungrammatical and fails to state restoration.
ghs.remedy: Use 'By the time her toes touch the floor, we're back to our usual selves.'

highlights.text: By the time the tip of her toes had touched the floor, it was as normal for us both.

rows.jp: 「ハーイ！」
rows.en: “Okaaay!”

ghs.en: Misato: "Yeee-s!"

rows.jp: 「先輩、聞いてください！」
rows.en: “Mimi, hear me out!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Senpai, please listen!"

rows.jp: 究極格闘技カラデ、その正拳側中段突きの構えを取る。
rows.en: I assume the stance of the Sideways Mid-Level Straight Punch, a technique of the ultimate martial art karade.

ghs.en: I took the Direct Horizontal Straight Punch posture of the 『Ultimate Unarmed Martial Art * Karade』.

rows.jp: ※正拳側中段突き――
rows.en: * Sideways Mid-Level Straight Punch—

rows.jp: 真横への正拳。カラデにおいては全方位の攻撃は基本であり、特に正拳突きは背後をのぞく広範囲を制する。
rows.en: A straight punch thrown directly sideways. In karade, omnidirectional attack is fundamental, and the straight punch in particular commands a broad area in every direction but the rear.

rows.jp: 同様にカラデには通常格闘技では想定されない、真上ならび真下への技も存在する。
rows.en: Karade also includes techniques aimed straight up and straight down, directions no conventional martial art would ever anticipate.

rows.jp: そんな奇天烈な攻撃をしてくる相手が地球上の生命体でないのはまず確実だが、備えあれば憂いなし。
rows.en: Any opponent attacking from such preposterous angles is almost certainly not a life-form native to Earth, but there is no harm in being prepared.

ghs.en:
While this most odd form of attack finds most
certainly no opponent or rival among the life
forms of this Earth, preparation is the key
to success.

rows.jp: 万一そのような敵を前にしたときはカラデのみが唯一抗しうるのは確実であり、まさにある意味最強。すべて世はメタゲームなのである。
rows.en: Should such an enemy ever appear, karade would unquestionably be the only art capable of resisting it and thus, in a sense, the strongest. Everything in this world is a metagame.

rows.jp: 四股を踏む相撲取りみたいな格好だが気にしない。
rows.en: I look like a sumo wrestler stamping his feet, but I pay that no mind.

ghs.en: It has a form similar to that of a sumo wrestler ceremonially raising and then stomping his feet, but let's not worry about that.

rows.jp: 「な、なんですか？」
rows.en: “W-what is it?”

ghs.en: Misato: "Wha-, what is it?"

rows.jp: 先輩も何かわけのわからない構えを取る。
rows.en: Mimi assumes some incomprehensible stance of her own.

ghs.en: Senpai also takes the stance of something with a meaning I couldn't comprehend.
ghs.assessment: The source says Senpai also adopts some incomprehensible stance. 'The stance of something with a meaning' changes the stance itself into an object belonging to something.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Senpai assumes some equally incomprehensible stance.'

highlights.text: Senpai also takes the stance of something with a meaning I couldn't comprehend.

rows.jp: 「今までさぼっていた部活に参加したいと思いました、オス！」
rows.en: “I have decided to participate in the club I have neglected until now! Osu!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I wish to participate in the club activities I have been dodging until now. Oss!"

rows.jp: 「なんですってー！？」
rows.en: “You whaaat?!”

ghs.en: Misato: "Whaaat did you say?!"

rows.jp: 「スク水からアンスコまで、黒須太一はあなたの部活ライフをいやらしくサポートします！」
rows.en: “From school swimsuits to undershorts, Taichi Kurosu will support your club life in the most indecent manner imaginable!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "From school swimsuits 'till the plain underwear worn over panties in sports (bloomers), Kurosu Taichi will offer his disgustingly lascivious support to your Club Activity Life!"
ghs.assessment: アンスコ is a compact term for athletic undershorts. The English inserts a long explanatory parenthesis into spoken dialogue, calls them plain underwear over panties, and disrupts the boast's rhythm.
ghs.remedy: Use a concise term such as 'athletic undershorts' without an in-dialogue gloss.

highlights.text: Taichi: "From school swimsuits 'till the plain underwear worn over panties in sports (bloomers), Kurosu Taichi will offer his disgustingly lascivious support to your Club Activity Life!"

rows.jp: 「想像するだにめまいがしますね！」
rows.en: “The mere thought makes me dizzy!”

ghs.en: Misato: "I am getting the giddies from imagining that!"
ghs.assessment: The source says merely imagining it makes her dizzy. 'The giddies' is not standard English and can suggest excitement rather than vertigo.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Just imagining it makes me dizzy!'

highlights.text: Misato: "I am getting the giddies from imagining that!"

rows.jp: 「恐悦！」
rows.en: “I am honored!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "A terrifying rejoice of delight is in I!"
ghs.assessment: 恐悦 is a terse, mock-formal 'I am delighted/honored.' 'A terrifying rejoice of delight is in I' is ungrammatical and misreads the first character as terror.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I am honored!'

highlights.text: Taichi: "A terrifying rejoice of delight is in I!"

rows.jp: 「誉めているように聞こえましたか！」
rows.en: “Did that sound like praise to you?!”

ghs.en: Misato: "Did you hear that as a compliment now!"
ghs.assessment: The source asks whether that sounded like praise. 'Did you hear that as a compliment now' is awkward and adds an unsupported 'now.'
ghs.remedy: Use 'Did that sound like a compliment to you?!'

highlights.text: Misato: "Did you hear that as a compliment now!"

rows.jp: 「他に理解のしようがありませんでした！」
rows.en: “There was no other possible interpretation!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "There exist no possible ways for contemplating other interpretations!"

rows.jp: 「すっごく頭いいです！　あまりにも良すぎたため、一回転してもはやおバカちゃんに戻ったのではないかと疑いました！」
rows.en: “You're so terribly clever! So clever I began to suspect you'd gone full circle and come out an idiot again!”

ghs.en: Misato: "You are sooo intelligent! You are so very intelligent, in fact, that I suspect you made an entire revolution back into being a complete idiot!"

rows.jp: 「天才と我々は紙一重だと言いますからナー！」
rows.en: “They say there's only a fine line between genius and people like us!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "The difference between Us and a genius is what could be called paper-thin, then!"

rows.jp: 変なポーズのまま、変な会話に興じる二人。
rows.en: Still holding our bizarre poses, we revel in our bizarre conversation.

ghs.en: The two of us amuse ourselves in weird conversations while we pose in weird ways.

rows.jp: うん、これぞ部活。
rows.en: Yes. This is club life.

ghs.en: Yes, this is what club activities are.

rows.jp: 「さあ、オイル塗りからバストマッサージ、野いちご狩りまで幅広くこなすこの愛肉奴隷めに、なんなりとお命じください」
rows.en: “Now command this devoted slave of flesh as you please. From oiling and bust massage to picking wild strawberries, no service lies beyond my broad expertise.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Indeed, from a oil-coated bust massage to wild strawberry hunting, your worthless meat-love slave has a wide range of uses, so order however you please!"
ghs.assessment: The source lists oiling, bust massage, and wild-strawberry picking as separate services. 'From a oil-coated bust massage' combines the first two and uses the wrong article.
ghs.remedy: Use 'From oiling to bust massage to wild-strawberry picking...'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Indeed, from a oil-coated bust massage to wild strawberry hunting, your worthless meat-love slave has a wide range of uses, so order however you please!"

rows.jp: 「まあ」
rows.en: “Well.”

ghs.en: Misato: "Well."

rows.jp: 調子に乗ってついＨなことを口走る。
rows.en: I get carried away and let something lewd slip out.

ghs.en: Caught up in the moment, my mouth runs off unconsciously into the perverted.

rows.jp: 先輩はＨなことに厳しいのだ（鈍いけど）。
rows.en: Mimi is strict about lewdness—although slow to notice it.

ghs.en: Senpai is very stern in regards to perversions (slow on the uptake though).

rows.jp: 幸いなることに、先輩はにっこり微笑んだ。
rows.en: Fortunately, she smiles sweetly.

ghs.en: Oh joyful event then, that Senpai is just smiling broadly.
ghs.assessment: The source says fortunately Senpai smiled. 'Oh joyful event then, that Senpai is just smiling' is an ungrammatical present-tense exclamation.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Fortunately, Senpai smiled brightly.'

highlights.text: Oh joyful event then, that Senpai is just smiling broadly.

rows.jp: 今のセクハラ発言に気づかなかったのか？
rows.en: Did she miss what I just said?

ghs.en: Did she not notice that sexually harassing utterance right there?

rows.jp: 天使の口唇が父なる神の慈愛を感じさせて告げた。
rows.en: Her angelic lips, radiant with the love of God the Father, proclaim:

ghs.en: Then, the lips of an angel that made me experience the kindness of God the Father announced:

rows.jp: 「ここからいなくなれ」
rows.en: “Get out of here.”

ghs.en: Misato: "Be ye forever gone from this place!"
ghs.assessment: The source bluntly says 'Get out of here.' 'Be ye forever gone' adds permanence and an archaic biblical register not present in her line.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Get out of here.'

highlights.text: Misato: "Be ye forever gone from this place!"

rows.jp: 「中国株に手を出したのが凋落(ちょうらく)のはじまりだったーっ！！」
rows.en: “Buying Chinese stocks was the beginning of my downfall!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "The moment I put my hands on that Chinese stock was the start of my life's ruiiin!!!"
ghs.assessment: 中国株 is Chinese stocks as a category. 'That Chinese stock' invents one particular share.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Getting into Chinese stocks was the beginning of my downfall!'

highlights.text: Taichi: "The moment I put my hands on that Chinese stock was the start of my life's ruiiin!!!"

rows.jp: フェンスの向こうに広がる無垢なる青空に生々しいことを叫んだ。
rows.en: I shout something painfully real into the innocent blue sky beyond the fence.

ghs.en: I make my rawly graphic shout towards that everexpanding everpure blue sky on the other side of the fence.
ghs.assessment: The source says he shouted something painfully real or vulgar at the pure sky. The English shifts to present, invents repeated 'ever' modifiers, and uses the nonstandard 'rawly.'
ghs.remedy: Use 'I shouted that painfully real thing at the pure blue sky beyond the fence.'

highlights.text: I make my rawly graphic shout towards that everexpanding everpure blue sky on the other side of the fence.

rows.jp: ま、机を食べないことで笑いを取れる中国人とか自体もういないけどな。
rows.en: Not that there are any Chinese people left who can get a laugh just by not eating a desk.

ghs.en: Well, Chinese people that can be laughed at for being able to eat anything on four legs but desks are themselves no longer among us anyway.

rows.jp: 「アンテナ、だいぶ形になりましたね」
rows.en: “The antenna has really taken shape.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "The antenna seems to have mostly taken shape, has it."
ghs.assessment: The source observes that the antenna has taken shape considerably. The tag 'has it' after 'seems' is malformed and weakens the direct observation.
ghs.remedy: Use 'The antenna has really taken shape.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "The antenna seems to have mostly taken shape, has it."

rows.jp: 「うん。頑張りました」
rows.en: “Yes. I worked hard.”

ghs.en: Misato: "Yes, I gave it my all!"

rows.jp: 平然と会話は続く。
rows.en: Our conversation continues without missing a beat.

ghs.en: The conversation continues normally.

rows.jp: ことほどさように、俺と先輩の関係性はとても強固なのだった。
rows.en: Such is the strength of the bond between Mimi and me.

ghs.en: As far as this goes, the nature of my relationship with Senpai is certainly strong.

rows.jp: 世界が滅亡したくらいでは壊れません。
rows.en: The end of the world is hardly enough to break it.

ghs.en: Even with the Fall of the World it did not break.
ghs.assessment: The source says even the world ending would not break their bond. 'Did not break' makes it a completed past test, while 'Fall of the World' turns destruction into an abstract title.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Even the end of the world won't break it.'

highlights.text: Even with the Fall of the World it did not break.

rows.jp: 「もう完成ですか？」
rows.en: “Is it finished?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Is it complete already?"

rows.jp: 「……まだ全然なんですよ、これが」
rows.en: “...Not even close, actually.”

ghs.en: Misato: "...not at all yet, it is not."
ghs.assessment: 'Not at all yet, it is not' duplicates the negative predicate and uses broken inversion.
ghs.remedy: Use '...Not even close yet.'

highlights.text: Misato: "...not at all yet, it is not."

rows.jp: 業者が組み立ててくれるはずだったアンテナ。
rows.en: A contractor was supposed to assemble the antenna.

ghs.en: The antenna should have been assembled by the contractors,

rows.jp: 搬入だけされて、うち捨てられた。
rows.en: Instead, they delivered it and abandoned it here.

ghs.en: but it was just brought in and then abandoned.

rows.jp: 「専門家じゃありませんし、だましだまし組み立ててます」
rows.en: “I'm no expert, so I've been cobbling it together through trial and error.”

ghs.en: Misato: "I am not a specialist, but by hook or by crook I am putting it together."
ghs.assessment: だましだまし means coaxing the work along or improvising. 'By hook or by crook' suggests unscrupulous means.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I'm no specialist, so I'm feeling my way through the assembly.'

highlights.text: Misato: "I am not a specialist, but by hook or by crook I am putting it together."

rows.jp: 「本体はいいとしても、配線や調整は手つかずですし」
rows.en: “The structure itself is one thing, but I haven't even begun the wiring or calibration.”

ghs.en: Misato: "The frame may be fine, but I have not laid hand on the wiring or the tuning."
ghs.assessment: 'Have not laid hand on' needs an article or idiomatic plural and is unnatural for untouched technical work.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I haven't touched the wiring or adjustments yet.'

highlights.text: Misato: "The frame may be fine, but I have not laid hand on the wiring or the tuning."

rows.jp: 「あらら」
rows.en: “Oh dear.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Oh my my."

rows.jp: 残念ながら、俺にもそういう知識はない。
rows.en: Unfortunately, I know nothing about that kind of work either.

ghs.en: Sad as it may be, I'm no expert on those things either.

rows.jp: 「……手伝えること、いやらしいサポート以外はなさそうですね」
rows.en: “...It doesn't sound as though there is anything I can help with, apart from indecent support.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...seems unlikely that I could help you outside of some disgustingly lascivious support then."

rows.jp: 「いやらしいサポートとかしたら停学にしますよ～」
rows.en: “If you offer any indecent support, I shall have you suspended.”

ghs.en: Misato: "Disgustingly lascivious support will entail a suspensio～n!"

rows.jp: なでっこなでっこ
rows.en: Pat, pat.

ghs.en: Sooooftly, sooooftly.
ghs.assessment: なでっこなでっこ represents repeated patting or stroking. 'Softly, softly' preserves only manner and omits the action.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Pat, pat.'

highlights.text: Sooooftly, sooooftly.

rows.jp: 頭をなでっこされる。
rows.en: She pats me on the head.

ghs.en: My head is sooooftly caressed.
ghs.assessment: The source says his head is patted or stroked. 'Caressed' makes the contact more sensual and does not echo the playful なでっこ.
ghs.remedy: Use 'She pats my head.'

highlights.text: My head is sooooftly caressed.

rows.jp: 「うるきゅー」
rows.en: “Urkyuu.”

rows.jp: 喉が鳴る。
rows.en: My throat rumbles.

ghs.en: A note from the throat.
ghs.assessment: The source says his throat makes a sound, suggesting a pleased purr. 'A note from the throat' is a verbless abstraction.
ghs.remedy: Use 'My throat rumbles contentedly.'

highlights.text: A note from the throat.

rows.jp: 「よしよし」
rows.en: “There, there.”

ghs.en: Misato: "Good boy good."
ghs.assessment: よしよし is repeated soothing praise, 'good, good.' 'Good boy good' adds 'boy' and reverses the second phrase's word order.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Good, good.'

highlights.text: Misato: "Good boy good."

rows.jp: 「うーうー」
rows.en: “Uu, uu.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Nnnh, nnnh..."

rows.jp: 「ホラ、部活ですし。その方が感じ出るかなって」
rows.en: “You know, this is a club. I thought it'd feel more like one that way.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Come on, this is club! Would that way not feel better?"
ghs.assessment: He says it is a club activity and doing it together would make it feel more like one. 'This is club' is ungrammatical, while 'feel better' changes authenticity into comfort.
ghs.remedy: Use 'It's a club activity, after all. Doing it together would make it feel more like one.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Come on, this is club! Would that way not feel better?"

rows.jp: 「で、でもですね、それはさすがにきついのではないかと」
rows.en: “B-but I think this may be beyond us.”

ghs.en: Misato: "B-, but, now, doing that would indeed be so very hard would it not."
ghs.assessment: The source tentatively says that would be rather difficult. 'Would indeed be so very hard would it not' piles two predicate structures together.
ghs.remedy: Use 'B-but wouldn't that be rather difficult?'

highlights.text: Misato: "B-, but, now, doing that would indeed be so very hard would it not."

rows.jp: 「やりようですね。そいつを攻略するのにもっとも適切な駒を使えばいいだけのことでありましょう」
rows.en: “That depends on how we approach it. We simply need to deploy the piece best suited to conquering the problem.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "There are ways. Capturing those guys merely requires making use of the most suitable pieces."
ghs.assessment: The source says it depends on the approach and one need only use the most suitable piece to overcome the target. 'Capturing those guys' pluralizes and personalizes the target without support.
ghs.remedy: Use 'It depends how you do it. Just use the piece best suited to overcoming the target.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "There are ways. Capturing those guys merely requires making use of the most suitable pieces."

rows.jp: 「三すくみにおけるナメクジを擁したカエルが蛇をも使役するに至ること示唆しているのと同じく、的確な人材によって急所を突くことが人間社会においては肝要であるわけでして」
rows.en: “Just as the frog in the three-way deadlock, armed with the slug, is thereby implied to command the snake as well, the essential thing in human society is to strike the weak point with precisely the right personnel.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "The same way that, in a three-way standoff, the frog that is home to a snail can then make it influence the snake into cooperation, it is of crucial importance inside human society to have the precise skills to strike at vital points."
ghs.assessment: The three-way-deadlock analogy has a frog armed with a slug go on to command the snake. 'Home to a snail' and 'influence the snake into cooperation' change both possession and control.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Just as a frog with a slug at its disposal can come to command the snake in a three-way deadlock...'

highlights.text: Taichi: "The same way that, in a three-way standoff, the frog that is home to a snail can then make it influence the snake into cooperation, it is of crucial importance inside human society to have the precise skills to strike at vital points."

rows.jp: 「理論的には、自分が支払える代価で手に入る駒をもっとも友好に使える局面に冷静にぶつけていけば制覇は成立しうるわけですから」
rows.en: “In theory, conquest becomes possible if we calmly direct every piece obtainable at a price we can pay into the situation where it will be most effective.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Because, theoretically speaking, if the pieces one has in hand because their price can be paid are employed with calm quietness to strike at the position most exploitable for a friendship, conquest must come into being."
ghs.assessment: The source says deploy affordable pieces calmly where they can be used most effectively. The English misreads effective use as 'exploitable for a friendship' and tangles acquisition, position, and conquest.
ghs.remedy: Use 'In theory, calmly deploy the pieces you can afford in the situations where they are most effective, and conquest becomes possible.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Because, theoretically speaking, if the pieces one has in hand because their price can be paid are employed with calm quietness to strike at the position most exploitable for a friendship, conquest must come into being."

rows.jp: 「無論、チャートが進むに従って管理の煩雑さと管理者の育成・配置といった新しい要素も混入してくるわけですが」
rows.en: “Of course, as the strategy chart advances, new factors enter the equation: increasingly complex administration, the training and deployment of managers, and so on.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Of course, following the progress of the chart, as management grows more complex, the situation demands the addition of a new element: the rearing and stationing of a supervising administrator."
ghs.assessment: The source lists new factors such as training and deploying managers as the chart advances. The English collapses those plural functions into one 'supervising administrator.'
ghs.remedy: Use 'As the chart advances, new factors enter, including increasingly complex management and the training and placement of managers.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Of course, following the progress of the chart, as management grows more complex, the situation demands the addition of a new element: the rearing and stationing of a supervising administrator."

rows.jp: 「ここいらになってくるとマキャベリズムにも触れる必要が出てきます」
rows.en: “At that stage, it becomes necessary to touch upon Machiavellianism.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "However, as we proximate to this area, it becomes a necessity to touch upon Machiavellism."
ghs.assessment: 'As we proximate to this area' is not idiomatic English, and the established term is Machiavellianism rather than 'Machiavellism.'
ghs.remedy: Use 'At this point, we also need to touch on Machiavellianism.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "However, as we proximate to this area, it becomes a necessity to touch upon Machiavellism."

ghs.assessment: The source says Peke-kun seems extremely evil. 'Got so very evilish' changes appearance into a past transformation and uses a malformed adjective.

highlights.text: Misato: "Peke-kun got so very evilish..."

highlights.text: Condemn it!

rows.jp: 空疎な饒舌さが求められている昨今の僕ら事情にあわせて無駄な読書ばかりしてきたせいか、ついリコーダー的に再生がかかってしまった。
rows.en: Perhaps all the useless reading I have done to keep pace with an age that demands hollow volubility has caused it to play back through me automatically, like a recorder.

ghs.en: Perhaps as the outcome of having done nothing but reading garbage in order to adapt to the circumstances that demand groundless garrulity of us young boys of today, I have stupidly and unconsciously played like a tape recorder.

rows.jp: 先輩の前では、素直な僕でいいのに！
rows.en: Around Mimi, I can just be my honest little self!

ghs.en: When in front of Senpai I should be a most upfront manservant!
ghs.assessment: 僕 here is the narrator's humble 'me.' 'Manservant' assigns a servant role absent from the source and changes his wish to be his honest self.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I can just be my honest self in front of Senpai!'

highlights.text: When in front of Senpai I should be a most upfront manservant!

rows.jp: ということで誤魔化すことにした。

ghs.en: And for that purpose, I've decided to swindle her.
ghs.assessment: 誤魔化す means cover it up or bluff his way past it. 'Swindle' implies deliberate fraud, often for money, and overstates the act.
ghs.remedy: Use 'So I decided to bluff my way out of it.'

highlights.text: And for that purpose, I've decided to swindle her.

highlights.text: Taichi: "AHH! My head...!"

highlights.text: Misato: "Ahhh, steadfast!"

ghs.en:
Under present conditions, the only person not to
have taken some form of mental damage would be...

rows.jp: 曜子ちゃんくらいのものか。
rows.en: it may be Yoko alone.

rows.jp: あと……あの娘。
rows.en: And... that girl.

ghs.en: And... that girl.

rows.jp: ……はて？
rows.en: ...Wait.

ghs.en: ...what even...?
ghs.assessment: はて is a puzzled 'hmm/wait.' 'What even' is an unfinished colloquial question with no object.
ghs.remedy: Use '...Hmm?'

highlights.text: ...what even...?

rows.jp: わからない。
rows.en: I don’t know.

ghs.en: I don't get that.
ghs.assessment: The source simply says 'I don't know.' 'I don't get that' adds a specific object and frames it as comprehension.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I don't know.'

highlights.text: I don't get that.

rows.jp: わかるのは。
rows.en: All I know is this:

ghs.en: What I get is,
ghs.assessment: わかるのは means 'what I do know is.' 'What I get is' suggests comprehension or acquisition and is awkward before the continuation.
ghs.remedy: Use 'What I do know is...'

highlights.text: What I get is,

rows.jp: 曜子ちゃんと似ているような、別物のような。
rows.en: She seems like Yoko, and yet like something else entirely.

ghs.en: she's something like Youko-chan, a special case.
ghs.assessment: The source says the girl seems similar to Youko yet also seems like something different. 'A special case' removes that similarity-versus-difference tension.
ghs.remedy: Use 'She seemed like Youko-chan, yet also like something entirely different.'

highlights.text: she's something like Youko-chan, a special case.

rows.jp: そんな違和感だけだ。
rows.en: Nothing beyond that sense of dissonance.

ghs.en: There's just that sense of physical discomfort.
ghs.assessment: 違和感 is a general sense of incongruity or something being off. 'Physical discomfort' incorrectly narrows it to bodily sensation.
ghs.remedy: Use 'That faint sense that something was off was all I had.'

highlights.text: There's just that sense of physical discomfort.

rows.jp: 『今』の俺では、それが限度だった。
rows.en: For the me of “now,” that was the limit.

ghs.en: That was the limit for myself as I am right now.

rows.jp: さておき。
rows.en: In any case.

ghs.en: All that aside.

rows.jp: 曜子ちゃんが、人類が消失したくらいで動揺するはずない。
rows.en: The disappearance of humanity would hardly be enough to disturb Yoko.

ghs.en:
There is no expectation that Youko-chan
would become discomposed, not even with
the disappearance of humanity.

rows.jp: 「今までの生活を、繰り返すしかできないんですよ」
rows.en: “All we can do is repeat the lives we lived before.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "There's nothing else that we can do but to repeat the same life we have had until now."
Misato: "..."

rows.jp: 先輩は深刻な顔をした。
rows.en: Mimi's expression turns grave.

ghs.en: Senpai's face turned serious.

rows.jp: 俺はことさら相好を崩した。
rows.en: I deliberately break into a broad smile.

ghs.en: I was letting my face deliberately fall into an especially beaming smile.
ghs.assessment: The source says he deliberately breaks into a broad smile. 'Was letting my face ... fall into' is progressive and physically awkward.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I deliberately broke into a broad smile.'

highlights.text: I was letting my face deliberately fall into an especially beaming smile.

rows.jp: 「だから俺も通学とかしてみました！」
rows.en: “So I decided to try going to school too!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "And that is why I have given going to school a try!"

rows.jp: 「あとハラキリ冬子も来てましたよ」
rows.en: “Harakiri Touko was there as well.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Also, Harakiri Touko has come in as well."
ghs.assessment: The source says Touko was there too. 'Has come in as well' uses an awkward present-perfect arrival construction.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Harakiri Touko was here too.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Also, Harakiri Touko has come in as well."

rows.jp: 「桐原さんも？」
rows.en: “Kirihara too?”

ghs.en: Misato: "Kirihara-san, too?"

rows.jp: 「座ってぼんやりとしてました」
rows.en: “She was sitting there in a daze.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "She was just sitting and spacing out."

rows.jp: 「そうですか……」
rows.en: “I see...”

ghs.en: Misato: "So she was..."

rows.jp: 「まあ、桜庭とか友貴とかは、そのうち補正されていくと思いますけど」
rows.en: “Well, I think Sakuraba and Tomoki will adjust in time.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Well, Sakuraba and Tomoki will eventually swing back, I think."

rows.jp: 「あいつらはなんだかんだいって健全に近いんで」
rows.en: “For all their faults, those two are almost healthy.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Say what you like, but those guys are close to that wholesome healthiness."
ghs.assessment: The source says they are close to healthy or normal. 'Close to that wholesome healthiness' is redundant and oddly deictic.
ghs.remedy: Use 'For all their quirks, they're pretty close to normal.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Say what you like, but those guys are close to that wholesome healthiness."

rows.jp: 「……そうだといいですねぇ」
rows.en: “...I hope so.”

ghs.en: Misato: "...that would be good, yes."

rows.jp: 少しためらって、目尻を下げる。
rows.en: After a moment's hesitation, her eyes soften.

ghs.en: With just a bit of hesitation, the corners of Senpai's eyes fall into a happier look.

rows.jp: 無理しているとわかった。
rows.en: I can tell she is forcing herself.

ghs.en: She was forcing herself, that I understood.

rows.jp: 頑張って、明るく振る舞っている。
rows.en: Straining to remain cheerful.

ghs.en: Doing her best to keep up that bright cheerful behavior.

rows.jp: 胸が痛んだ。
rows.en: My chest aches.

ghs.en: My heart ached.

rows.jp: 「……じゃあ、何か手伝えることがあったら言ってください」
rows.en: “...Then please tell me if there is anything I can do to help.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...then, if there is anything I can help with, please say the word."

rows.jp: 「あ、はい、そのときは」
rows.en: “Oh. Yes, when the time comes.”

ghs.en: Misato: "Ah, yes, if that time comes..."

rows.jp: 「是非に」
rows.en: “Please do.”

ghs.en: Misato: "Without fail!"

rows.jp: 夏日の下。
rows.en: Beneath the summer sun.

ghs.en: Under this Summer sun,

rows.jp: 先輩を残して、俺は去った。
rows.en: I leave Mimi behind.

ghs.en: Senpai remained, while I departed,

rows.jp: 鉄扉をこじあけて校舎に入る。
rows.en: I force open the steel door and step back inside the school.

ghs.en: closing the iron door and reentering the school building.
ghs.assessment: The source says he pries the metal door open and enters the building. 'Closing the iron door' states the opposite action.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I pry open the metal door and enter the school building.'

highlights.text: closing the iron door and reentering the school building.

rows.jp: 振り返ると、彼女はずっと見送ってくれていた。
rows.en: When I look back, she is still watching me go.

ghs.en: I look back and I can see that she has been watching me leave all along.
ghs.assessment: The source is past narration: he looked back and saw she had watched him leave. The English shifts the first two actions to present.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I looked back and saw that she had been watching me leave all along.'

highlights.text: I look back and I can see that she has been watching me leave all along.
